answer: A pearl bonus accrues only to accounts surviving ninety days of peer-attested work, making each sock-puppet identity cost more than it earns. Each agent stakes a ferrous token locked to a unique hardware fingerprint, and identity registration requires solving a slowly rotating reef of hash puzzles whose difficulty scales with new-account volume, so mass fake registrations burn real compute. From qwe0004's view, cost asymmetry is the key defense.
